part_title: CloudFormation Template Lifecycle, Change Sets and Stack Safety

scenes.title: CloudFormation lifecycle
scenes.narration: This slide walks through a declarative CloudFormation deployment from template authoring to outputs. First, write a YAML or JSON template that describes resources such as S3 buckets, IAM roles, Lambda functions and databases. Instead of issuing imperative create commands for every service, you declare the desired state. The next stage is a change set that previews whether the update will add, modify, remove or replace resources. Read the replacement warning closely: some property changes create a new physical resource and can cause disruption or data loss if state migration is not planned. When the change set is executed, CloudFormation uses resource dependencies to provision in an appropriate order, and stack events show the progress. Outputs can publish selected resource identifiers and endpoints for other components. The lower panels cover rollback, drift detection and retention rules. Rollback attempts recovery after failed updates; drift detection reports supported differences introduced outside the template; DeletionPolicy and UpdateReplacePolicy help control what happens to stored data when resources are deleted or replaced. IaC enables repeatability, but only careful change review makes updates safe.
